title: Stack vs heap

blocks.md:
## Where values live

The **stack** is the list of function calls that are running now. The **heap** is the bag of objects those frames point at. A stack frame is short-lived. A heap object stays as long as something still points at it.

A closure keeps a heap object alive after the stack frame that created it is gone. `await` *pauses that function* — it does not freeze the operating system.

On the desk: the fox calls `outer()`, which calls `inner()`. While `inner` runs, it sits on top of the stack. The beacon record it points at lives on the heap. A later `then` can still read that record after `inner` has returned.

choices.md: Stops the whole computer until the promise finishes
Pauses that function and lets other JS run

blocks.promptMd: `await` freezes the whole computer until the promise finishes.
blocks.explainMd: Only that async function pauses. Other JavaScript on the page can still run. The operating system is not frozen.

description: Calls sit on a stack. Objects live on the heap until nothing points at them.
